# AGENTS.md

Guidance for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, …) working in this repository. This is the single source of truth: `.claude/CLAUDE.md` only imports it. Edit this file, not that one.

## Project

"aipocalypse" — a PC first-person shooter built in Unity **6000.6.7f1** (Unity 6) with URP 17.6. Development happens in the Unity Editor; the `*.csproj`/`*.slnx` files at the repo root are generated by Unity — never edit them.

**Performance target: 60 fps at 1080p on an RTX 2060-class GPU** (16.6 ms per frame, CPU and GPU). Judge perf work against it, measured in a build or with the editor overhead accounted for (`unity-optimization-pc`).

**Polish levels:** each area has an effort level (Very High / High / Medium / Low) in `docs/ROADMAP.md` → "Polish levels". Scale work to it, and ask before polishing an area beyond its level.

**Editor control: Unity CLI** (`unity`, via the `com.unity.pipeline` package). The deprecated Unity MCP is not used. The CLI's docs ship with the package in `Library/PackageCache/com.unity.pipeline@*/Documentation~/` (`commands/`, `authoring-commands.md`, `testing.md`, …); in Claude Code, also load the official `unity:unity-cli` skill. Read them before editor work.

```bash
P="$(cygpath -w "$PWD")"                                    # Git Bash: the CLI doesn't match /d/... paths
unity status --project-path "$P"                            # not ready: Safe Mode (unity pipeline list) or ask the user to open the project
unity command --project-path "$P" editor set_auto_tick --enable true   # commands stall while Unity is unfocused otherwise
unity command --project-path "$P" script recompile          # then poll until completed / up_to_date:
unity command --project-path "$P" script recompile_status
unity command --project-path "$P" console status            # console get for the messages
unity command --project-path "$P" test run --mode editor
bash .claude/hooks/check-undeclared-packs.sh                # vendor folders missing from ASSETS/PLUGINS.md
```

- Drive the live editor with `unity command` (scenes, GameObjects, components, prefabs, assets, captures, console) instead of hand-editing `.unity`/`.prefab`/`.asset` YAML: `script run` for bulk/plugin work, `script eval` for one-liners, `capture scene_view` to check results. `unity command` lists the groups, `unity command <group>` a group's commands. Older docs may use pre-rename flat names (`run_script`, `run_tests`, `set_autotick`); the CLI error names the replacement.
- Only one agent drives the editor at a time. When two agents work in parallel, use separate branches/worktrees.

**Editor gotchas** (learned the hard way):

- Play mode freezes while the editor is unfocused (`runInBackground` is off): after entering play, `script eval` `Application.runInBackground = true` (runtime only, not saved).
- Keyboard/mouse reach the game only while the Game view has focus. For scripted play tests drive input with a virtual gamepad (`InputSystem.AddDevice<Gamepad>` + `QueueStateEvent`).
- Right after `script recompile`, poll `script recompile_status` before anything else; a command during the domain reload fails with "Connection reset by server".
- The first frame after a `script run` includes its in-memory compile (~0.5 s): skip it when measuring. For clean editor perf numbers hide the Hierarchy window (it rebuilds per change and spikes with ~16k objects).
- `capture game_view --save_path` resolves under `Assets/` and imports the image: delete it with `AssetDatabase.DeleteAsset` afterwards.
- In Git Bash, heredocs containing an apostrophe break; write edit scripts to a file and run that.
- `test run` blocks the editor on a modal "Scene(s) Have Been Modified" dialog when an open scene is dirty (the CLI just times out). Check `SceneManager.GetActiveScene().isDirty` first and ask the user before discarding anything.
- The EditMode test assembly is editor-only, so its MonoBehaviours can't be added to GameObjects; a test component goes in the PlayMode test assembly (see `ControllerHitRelay`).

## Skills

Skills live in **`.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`** (Codex reads this path; `.claude/skills` is a symlink to it — needs `git config core.symlinks true` and Windows Developer Mode on each clone). **Before working in an area below, read the matching `SKILL.md`** (and its `references/` when it points there). They are checked against the installed package sources; where a skill conflicts with this file or `docs/technicals/`, the project docs win.

| Skill | Read before |
| --- | --- |
| `aipocalypse-architecture` | Registrations, scopes, installers, injection; gameplay events (MessagePipe); any async/await, delays, pause; C# touching serialization, statics, play-mode hooks, build defines or Unity 6.6 APIs |
| `aipocalypse-enemy-ai` | Any enemy/companion/animal/NPC movement or AI decision, and designing behaviours: EnemySystem, Behavior Designer Pro trees ticked by `EnemyManager` and built from text specs (`TreeKit`), A* `FollowerEntity`, navmesh, spawning, the GDD behaviour catalogue and AI building blocks |
| `aipocalypse-characters` | Adding, swapping or animating any character model (enemy, NPC, companion, animal), from any vendor: model vs entity prefab, the animator parameter contract and `CharacterKit`, `EnemyAnimator`, verifying looks and animation |
| `tools-unity-feel` | Game feel / feedbacks (allowed vs banned feedbacks; points to Feel's own skills) |
| `tools-unity-broaudio` | Any sound, music or ambience: `AudioService`, `SoundID`s, BroAudio libraries (points to BroAudio's `CLAUDE.md`) |
| `tools-unity-audio-tools` | Editing audio clips in the editor: trim, normalize, fade, export (points to Audio Tools' own skills) |
| `tools-unity-text-studio` | Animated / typewriter text (Text Studio is Undecided: ask first; points to its own skills) |
| `tools-unity-map-generation` | Building or changing a map: layout from a concept, generated heights/water/vegetation/boundary/dressing, rebuilds, map art packs and perf, and how MicroVerse is used here (the WorldMap generator; step runner and MicroVerse kit in `scripts/`) |
| `tools-unity-stylized-water` | Any Stylized Water 3 work: water bodies, RiverModeler rivers, waterfalls, underwater, height queries, water materials and perf |
| `tools-unity-shader-graph` | Any shader or material effect: creating or editing Shader Graphs (agents use its `ShaderGraphKit`), copying vendor graphs into `_Game`, AllIn1 Shader Nodes, custom HLSL nodes, shader values driven from C#, keywords and variants |
| `tools-unity-synty-characters` | Synty characters and clips: building / customizing Sidekick characters without the window (`SidekickKit`), Sidekick and Polygon packs, Base / Goblin Locomotion clips, vendor traps |
| `tools-unity-animation-rigging` | Any IK, aim / look-at, hand-on-weapon, foot grounding, secondary motion, arms / forearms or rig-driven clip work: Animation Rigging rigs built from code, manual evaluation, baking rigs into clips (`RigKit`), Control Rig Pro and its traps |

The project skills hold only what is specific to this repo. Library detail lives in generic user-scope skills in Claude Code (`~/.claude/skills/`): `unity-vcontainer`, `unity-messagepipe`, `unity-unitask`, `unity-6-new-apis`, `unity-behavior-designer-pro`, `unity-astar`, `unity-microverse`, and `unity-optimization-pc` for measuring or optimising performance. The project skills point to them; when they are not available (other agents, other machines), read the package source under `Packages/` or `Library/PackageCache/` instead of guessing.

To add a skill: create `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with `name` and `description` frontmatter, and add a row here. The `tools-unity-*` skills started from [tjboudreaux/cc-plugin-unity-gamedev](https://github.com/tjboudreaux/cc-plugin-unity-gamedev) (MIT, `.agents/skills/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSE-unity-gamedev.txt`).

## Where things live

- `Assets/_Game/` — **all first-party game code and content go here**: systems in `_Core/` (Features depend on Core, never the reverse), content per thing in `Content/<Kind>/<Name>/`, settings ScriptableObjects in `Data/<System>/`, per-map assets in `Maps/<Map>/`. Full layout, asmdefs, system ownership and the prototype → main game rules: `docs/technicals/ARCHITECTURE.md`; script map: `docs/technicals/CODE_STRUCTURE.md`.
- `Assets/_Game/Scenes/Prototypes/WorldMap.unity` — the prototype world map where mechanics are tested (Build Settings list no scenes yet). Prototype scenes use the real code and prefabs, never copies.
- `Assets/_StoreAssets/` and `Assets/Synty/` — third-party art/asset-store content. Treat as vendor code: don't modify; reference or make variants/prefabs under `_Game`. Content packs: `docs/technicals/ASSETS.md`; code plugins and tools: `docs/technicals/PLUGINS.md`.
- `Assets/_Placeholder/` — temporary storage for placeholder and AI-generated assets (e.g. borrowed audio). Tagged Avoid in ASSETS.md: nothing ships from here, don't add new references from `_Game`, and replace the existing ones with real assets.
- `Assets/Plugins/` — third-party editor/runtime tooling (Odin Inspector, DOTween/Demigiant, GPUInstancerPro, etc.). Don't modify.
- `Assets/_Game/Settings/` — the live URP assets (`PC_RPAsset`, `PC_Renderer`), volume profile, Input System config, audio import presets. `Assets/Settings/` holds only the Build Profiles and an unused URP global settings asset.
- `Packages/` — embedded vendor packages (A*, GPU Instancer Pro, Behavior Designer Pro, COZY, MicroVerse, Spline Spawner, SC Screen Effects); treat as vendor code, listed in PLUGINS.md.
- `AgentScripts/` — editor scripts outside `Assets/`, run with `unity command script run` (the map generator in `AgentScripts/Maps/<Map>/`, setup, review and perf scripts per feature). `Tools/` holds the same kind of one-off editor script (e.g. `HandFistReview.cs`).

## Key tech choices (from `Packages/manifest.json`)

- **Input**: new Input System only (`activeInputHandler: 1`). Actions asset is `Assets/_Game/Settings/InputSystem_Actions.inputactions`: `Player` map (Move, Look, Attack, Interact, Crouch, Jump, Previous, Next, Sprint, Slot1–Slot9, Drop, Aim, Reload), `UI`, plus `Debug` and `Console` maps for editor and dev builds (keys in DEBUG.md / CONSOLE.md). Use these actions; don't call the legacy `UnityEngine.Input`. Game code reads input only through `InputService` (root scope, generated wrapper `GameInputActions`); never enable/disable actions or set the cursor lock elsewhere.
- **Architecture / DI**: VContainer (`jp.hadashikick.vcontainer`) + UniTask. Cross-system events go through MessagePipe. No `X.Instance` singletons in game code — services are plain C# registered in lifetime scopes; each system registers through its own installer. Entity prefabs (player, enemies…) carry their own `EntityScope` and must work dropped into any scene. See `docs/technicals/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
- **AI**: Behavior Designer Pro 3.3 trees for every agent; crowd enemy trees ticked time-sliced by `EnemyManager`.
- **Enemy navigation**: A* Pathfinding Project 5.4 (`FollowerEntity` agents).
- **Camera**: Cinemachine 6.6 (Cinemachine 3 API, namespace `Unity.Cinemachine`).
- **Rendering/perf**: URP, GPU Instancer Pro for foliage/props, VFX Graph, Splines, Terrain Tools.

## Plugins and content packs — check before building, use them correctly

Many plugins (Feel, BroAudio, Easy Save 3, Damage Numbers Pro, DOTween, Odin, Localization…) and art, UI, VFX and audio packs are installed. **Read `docs/technicals/PLUGINS.md` before any task that a plugin might cover, and `docs/technicals/ASSETS.md` before building, dressing or sounding anything.**

Both files declare each package once, with one tag: **Must** (the only choice), **Should** (the default), **Could** (fallback for what the higher tags lack), **Maybe** (last resort, ask first), **Avoid** (reference only, nothing in `_Game` points at it), **Undecided** (ask first). Pick the highest-tagged package that has what you need; using a lower one means writing why in its row.

- **Check first:** before writing a system or tool, check whether an installed plugin already does it. Use the plugin rather than reinventing it, unless PLUGINS.md says otherwise.
- **Use it the documented way:** follow the plugin's rules in PLUGINS.md (e.g. no plugin singletons/static event systems in gameplay code, `TimeService` owns `Time.timeScale`, uGUI for UI, DOTween for code tweens, behavior trees for all AI with crowd trees ticked by `EnemyManager`). When unsure how a plugin works, read its docs or source in `Assets/Plugins/` / `Packages/` instead of guessing (some ship their own guide, e.g. `Assets/Plugins/BroAudio/CLAUDE.md`).
- **Use it efficiently:** prefer the plugin's pooling, batching and caching features (Damage Numbers Pro and BroAudio pooling, GPUI instancing) and keep per-instance plugin components off crowd entities (exceptions: BD `BehaviorTree` in Manual mode, A* `FollowerEntity`).
- **Before using assets, look for undeclared and Undecided packs:** whenever a task picks art, animation, UI, VFX or audio, compare `Assets/_StoreAssets/` with ASSETS.md and check the Undecided rows. If an undeclared or Undecided pack could serve the task, stop and ask the user: say what it contains, suggest a tag with a one-line reason, then add or update the row with their decision (Undecided if they don't decide) before using it then update the file.
- **Keep PLUGINS.md and ASSETS.md current:** when adding, removing or starting to use a plugin or pack in a new way (or for a new purpose), update its row in the same change. Each vendor folder (`_StoreAssets/<Kind>/<Pack>`, `Synty/<Pack>`, `Synty/SidekickCharacters/Characters/<Pack>`, `Plugins/<Name>`) must appear by its exact folder name. `bash .claude/hooks/check-undeclared-packs.sh` lists the ones that don't (Claude Code runs it at session start); for each, suggest a tag, ask the user, then add the row.

## Ask the user first

Stop and ask before:

- Implementing anything taken from `docs/gdd/` (see below), including `docs/gdd/IDEAS.md`.
- Adding a package, plugin or content pack, relying on one PLUGINS.md or ASSETS.md marks Undecided (e.g. Text Studio), or using one marked Avoid.
- Adding or renaming BroAudio entities/libraries (Library Manager authoring) or `SoundID`s.
- Renaming or moving a Behavior Designer task class (trees store its full type name).
- A full rebuild of an existing map, or changing a scene's structure (`WorldMap.unity`) beyond the task.
- Bringing in an art pack or style not already used.
- Anything destructive or outward-facing: deleting assets, rewriting history, pushing. Commit only when asked.

## Prompt first, GDD second

When writing code, the user's prompt is the spec.

- Build what the prompt asks. Don't add mechanics, rules or numbers the prompt didn't ask for.
- You may read `docs/gdd/` for context, but anything taken from it (a rule, a mechanic, a number, a constraint) must be **proposed and confirmed by the user before you implement it**. Say what it is and where it comes from (e.g. "CORE.md says stamina drains when sprinting — add it?").
- If the prompt and the GDD disagree, follow the prompt and mention the difference; don't "fix" the code toward the GDD.
- Technical docs (`docs/technicals/`, this file) still decide *how* to build.

## Keeping docs current

- When you add or change a core system (data structures, gameplay flow, system boundaries), update the relevant section of this file or `docs/` in the same change. Keep this file high-level; put detail in `docs/`.
- `docs/gdd/` — game design. Design intent: `docs/gdd/GDD.md` is the index of per-topic files; start with `docs/gdd/CORE.md` (pitch, pillars, core loop). `docs/gdd/IDEAS.md` is a draft scratchpad, not canon — never implement from it unless explicitly asked.
- `docs/technicals/` — one doc per system; read the one you touch: `ARCHITECTURE` (layout, data flow), `CODE_STRUCTURE` (script map — update whenever you add, move or remove a script), `PLUGINS`, `ASSETS`, `SYNTY_CATALOG` (Synty packs not yet imported), `UI` (HUD), `EQUIPMENT` (items, hotbar), `WEAPONS`, `HANDS` (first-person grips, poses, clips), `ENVIRONMENT` (world map), `DAYNIGHT`, `CONSOLE` (dev console, cheats), `DEBUG` (other debug tools).
- Current milestone/tasks: `docs/ROADMAP.md`.

## Code style

Base convention: the `oss-unity:csharp-unity` skill (Claude Code; other agents read `~/.claude/oss-skills/oss-unity/skills/csharp-unity/SKILL.md`). Read it before writing C#: early returns, one responsibility per class, cached lookups, GC-free hot paths, lifecycle and Unity 6 API rules. Its own house style yields to this file; **where they disagree, this section wins**:

- **Naming:** PascalCase types, methods, properties, public fields, consts and `static readonly`; `_camelCase` for every private field, serialized or not; camelCase locals and parameters; `I` prefix on interfaces; `Async` suffix on UniTask methods. No `m_` / `k_` / `s_` prefixes.
- Leave out `private` (it's the default) and don't write `this.`. Mark leaf classes `sealed`. No `#region`.
- **Serialized fields:** always `[SerializeField] T _field;` with a read-only property when other code needs it (`public T Field => _field;`). **Never `[field: SerializeField]` auto-properties**: their serialized name `<Field>k__BackingField` breaks on a rename and can't be found with `FindProperty("_field")`. Public fields only in nested `[Serializable]` data structs/classes and in pure data ScriptableObjects (styles, settings, definitions, profiles: assets that are only tuned in the Inspector and read by code). Runtime code never writes to those fields: in the editor the change would stick to the asset after Play.
- **Renaming or retyping a serialized field loses its saved values** on every asset, prefab and scene. Add `[FormerlySerializedAs("oldName")]`; to drop it later, reserialize the affected assets (`AssetDatabase.ForceReserializeAssets` via `script run`), check the new YAML against the old values (`git diff`), then remove the attribute. Also update anything that finds the field by name (`FindProperty`, reflection in tests and `AgentScripts/`).
- Formatting and naming are also in the root `.editorconfig` (Rider/VS apply it; severities are suggestions so the Unity console stays clean).
- Block-scoped namespaces matching the folder (CODE_STRUCTURE.md), `using` lines outside the namespace, braces on their own line; a single-statement `if`/loop body may drop its braces. `var` when the type is obvious.
- A `Tooltip` instead of a comment on serialized fields whose meaning or units aren't obvious.
- Async, cancellation, events and lookups follow `aipocalypse-architecture` (MessagePipe across systems, VContainer instead of `Find*`, no `destroyCancellationToken` on pooled objects), not the skill's generic advice.
- **Keep comments compact.** No XML/docstring blocks (`/// <summary>`), no long summaries. A class or method gets at most 1–2 short `//` lines stating its purpose, and none when the name already says it. Don't comment what the code plainly does.
- **No fix narration.** Don't leave comments about a bug fix or adjustment ("changed X to Y", "fixed bug", "was Z before"); that belongs in the commit message. Comment only a critical fix, a workaround or a non-obvious solution, in 1–2 lines that explain the *why*.
- Serialized key→value data uses Unity 6.6's built-in `[SerializeField] Dictionary<TKey, TValue>` ([manual](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.6/Documentation/Manual/script-serialization-dictionaries.html)), not a list of key/value structs or a custom `SerializableDictionary`. **Never use Odin serialization** (`SerializedMonoBehaviour`, `SerializedScriptableObject`, `[OdinSerialize]`, Odin serialized collections) in any case; Odin is for inspector attributes only.

## Testing

- Tests use `com.unity.test-framework` in `Assets/_Game/Tests/`: `EditMode/` (`Aipocalypse.Tests.EditMode`) for almost everything, `PlayMode/` (`WorldMapSmokeTests`) for scene smoke tests. Run with `unity command test run --mode editor`.
- Test what can break silently: rules in plain C# classes (stamina, recoil, jams, clock), enum-keyed data tables (every value has an entry, `PhaseDataTests`), and prefab/asset wiring (`ItemPrefabTests`). Name tests `Subject_ExpectedBehaviour` (`Deal_ReportsTheKillAndCapsDamageAtWhatWasLeft`).
- PlayMode runs through the CLI have reported "0/0 passed" without running anything. If so, verify play behaviour by entering play mode and probing with `script run` (plus `runInBackground` and a virtual gamepad), then stop.

## Before you finish

1. `script recompile` → `script recompile_status` is clean, and `console status` shows no new errors.
2. `test run --mode editor` passes, with tests added or updated for changed rules.
3. Changed editor content is checked (`capture scene_view`, `component get_fields`), not assumed.
4. Docs updated in the same change: CODE_STRUCTURE.md for any script added, moved or removed; PLUGINS.md / ASSETS.md for plugin or pack use; the system's doc for behaviour changes.
5. Report what was verified and what wasn't. Don't commit unless asked.

## Conventions / gotchas

- Commit messages: a one-line summary prefixed by the kind of change: `+ add <thing>`, `* <update/fix/refactor> <thing>`, `- remove <thing>` (e.g. `+ add vfx`, `* fix sky`, `- remove examples`).
- `.gitattributes` is the standard Unity template with Git LFS for binary asset types; make sure LFS is installed before committing/pulling large assets.
- Always commit `.meta` files together with their assets; never delete/rename asset files outside the Unity Editor (or move the `.meta` alongside) or GUID references break.
- Main branch is `develop`.
- Never name git branches in skills or docs (branches get deleted); describe the change or point at files on `develop`.
